title: Daniel Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Daniel 9: the seventy years understood from the books, Daniel's prayer of confession, and Gabriel's message of the seventy weeks.

questions.text: What did Daniel understand by the books, from Yahweh's word to Jeremiah the prophet?
questions.explanation: He understood by the books the number of the years about which Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah for the accomplishing of the desolations of Jerusalem, even seventy years.

answers.text: That Jerusalem would never be rebuilt
That the desolations of Jerusalem would be seventy years
That the city would fall in his own lifetime
That the kingdom would be given to the Medes

questions.text: How did Daniel set his face to seek the Lord God?
questions.explanation: He set his face to the Lord God to seek by prayer and petitions, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

answers.text: By offering sacrifices in the sanctuary
By sending messengers to the prophet Jeremiah
By reading the books aloud before the king
By prayer and petitions, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes

questions.text: Whom does the prayer say the people had not listened to?
questions.explanation: The prayer says, “We haven't listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers.”

answers.text: The judges who judged them
The priests of the sanctuary
God's servants the prophets
The kings of Judah

questions.text: What does the prayer say belongs to the Lord our God?
questions.explanation: The prayer says that to the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.

answers.text: Mercies and forgiveness
Confusion of face
The seventy years
The books of the prophets

questions.text: In whose law were the curse and the oath written that had been poured out on them?
questions.explanation: The prayer says the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on them, because they had sinned against him.

answers.text: The law of the Medes and Persians
The books of Jeremiah the prophet
The writing of truth
The law of Moses, the servant of God

questions.text: What did Daniel ask God to do for the sanctuary?
questions.explanation: He asked God to listen to the prayer of his servant and to cause his face to shine on his sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord's sake.

answers.text: To fill it again with the vessels taken to Babylon
To cause his face to shine on the sanctuary that is desolate
To measure it out again for the priests
To seal it up for many days still to come

questions.text: On what basis does the prayer say the petitions are presented before God?
questions.explanation: He says, “we do not present our petitions before you for our righteousness, but for your great mercies' sake.”

answers.text: Not for their own righteousness, but for God's great mercies
For the sake of the covenant with the kings of Judah
Because the seventy years were already finished
Because the people had turned from their iniquities

questions.text: Who came to Daniel while he was speaking in prayer?
questions.explanation: While he was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision at the beginning, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening offering.

answers.text: Michael, the prince of his people
A watcher and a holy one
The man Gabriel
A man clothed in linen with eyes like torches

questions.text: What are the seventy weeks decreed on Daniel's people and holy city to accomplish?
questions.explanation: They are decreed to finish disobedience, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.

answers.text: To number the years of the kings of Persia
To finish disobedience and bring in everlasting righteousness
To divide the land among the tribes by lot
To rebuild the sanctuary in seven days

questions.text: What will happen in the middle of the one week in which a firm covenant is made with many?
questions.explanation: He will make a firm covenant with many for one week, and in the middle of the week he will cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease.

answers.text: The city and the sanctuary will be rebuilt
The Anointed One will be anointed as prince
The seventy years will begin to be counted
The sacrifice and the offering will be caused to cease
